title: Power Automate process mining: Process Intelligence Studio for object-centric models
summary: Hold: the generic capacity-allocation instructions do not establish that Process Mining capacity is available through that admin UI. The description of the existing workspace also omits Learn's restriction that filters apply within the current tab.

claims.claim: This roadmap change belongs to Power Automate.
claims.quote: "products": ["Power Automate"]

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Web as the platform.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: General availability is targeted for October CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "October CY2026"

claims.claim: Preview is targeted for September CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "September CY2026"

claims.claim: The change is enabled automatically for admins, makers and marketers, supporting defaultState on.
claims.quote: Enabled for admins/makers/marketers automatically

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: Item-specific licensing changes or separate OCPM charges have not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: object-centric process mining OCPM licensing Process Intelligence Studio Power Automate Premium capacity; "object-centric" "licensing" Power Automate. Opened process-advisor-overview, object-centric-overview, object-centric-ingest-event-log and power-automate-licensing/types.
claims.fix: Keep licensing.model unknown for the incremental change, but replace licensing.notes and the first Cost and licensing sentence with: 'Additional licensing for this change is not yet published; the documented Power Automate process mining licensing remains the baseline.' This avoids implying that baseline process mining entitlement is unconfirmed.

claims.claim: The generic add-on allocation screen is reached through Licensing > Capacity add-ons > Summary > Add-ons > Manage.
claims.quote: On the navigation pane, select Licensing. In the Licensing pane, select Capacity add-ons. On the Capacity page, select the Summary tab. ... Scroll down to the Add-ons section, and select Manage.

claims.where: controls[0].ui: applicability to Process mining capacity
claims.claim: The generic add-on allocation UI specifically permits allocation of Process Mining capacity.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate process mining capacity allocation environment admin center ProcessMiningDataStorage; "process mining" "allocate" "capacity" "environment" "admin". Opened capacity-add-on and programmability-tutorial-allocate-capacity-addons; neither identifies Process Mining in the UI.
claims.fix: Set controls[0].ui to null and render that side as 'Not yet documented'. Keep its verified ProcessMiningDataStorage API call. The cited tutorial explicitly warns that not all add-ons are available in the admin UI, so the API enumeration alone does not establish UI availability.

claims.claim: PATCH licensing/environments/{environmentId}/allocations with api-version=2024-10-01 and currencyAllocations containing ProcessMiningDataStorage and allocated sets environment capacity.
claims.quote:
PATCH https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/environments/{environmentId}/allocations?api-version=2024-10-01
currencyAllocations | CurrencyAllocationRequestModelV1[]
allocated | integer (int32)
currencyType | ExternalCurrencyType
ProcessMiningDataStorage

claims.claim: Settings > Power Platform settings > Tenant settings > Add-on capacity assignments > Only specific admins restricts who can allocate add-on capacity.
claims.quote: In the title bar, select the Settings icon. ... Select Power Platform settings. ... On the Tenant settings page, select Add-on capacity assignments, and then select Only specific admins.

claims.claim: Set-TenantSettings accepts -RequestBody with a tenant-settings object; the displayed call uses a real cmdlet and parameter.
claims.quote:
Module: Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell Module
Set-TenantSettings
    [-RequestBody] <Object>
The Set-TenantSettings cmdlet updates tenant settings in Power Platform.
-RequestBody
Tenant settings to be updated.

claims.claim: The Boolean tenant setting disableCapacityAllocationByEnvironmentAdmins disables allocation by environment administrators when true.
claims.quote: disableCapacityAllocationByEnvironmentAdmins | Boolean | Ability to disable capacity allocation by environment administrators. Default value is false.

claims.claim: The page documenting the capacity-allocation tenant-setting definition is marked preview.
claims.quote:
List tenant settings (preview)
[This article is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.]

claims.where: controls[2].ui and controls[2].api; Governance controls prose
claims.claim: No separate admin UI or automation switch for Process Intelligence Studio or object-centric models was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate Process Intelligence Studio object-centric process mining enable disable admin environment setting Power Platform API PowerShell pac admin; "Process Intelligence Studio" "disable"; "object-centric process mining" "enable" "settings". Opened studio overview and OCPM ingestion.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls prose
claims.claim: Process mining access relies on environment security and process-related Dataverse permissions.
claims.quote: The process mining capability relies on environment security and Microsoft Dataverse security roles and privileges to grant access to its features in Power Automate.

claims.claim: The event-log storage source introduces access requirements for process mining.
claims.quote:
all users that have the Owner or Co-Owner role on the process must be attributed:
Storage Blob Data Reader or Storage Blob Data Contributor role assigned
Azure Resource Manager Reader role assigned, at minimum.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/process-mining-byo-azure-data-lake and https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/process-mining-files-fabric-onelake to sources for the statement about source-dependent access requirements.

claims.claim: The process intelligence experience is a customisable analysis workspace in Power Automate Process Mining.
claims.quote: The new process intelligence experience is the next-generation interface for process analysis in Power Automate Process Mining. It delivers a comprehensive, customizable dashboard for exploring process intelligence insights.

claims.claim: The workspace supports multiple tabs for different analytical perspectives.
claims.quote: Multiple tabs for organizing different analytical perspectives

claims.where: summary; What's changing: tiles and layouts
claims.claim: Cards can be arranged in customisable grid layouts.
claims.quote:
Customizable layouts where you can arrange, resize, and configure cards
The main canvas displays multiple cards arranged in a grid layout.

claims.where: What's changing: filters applied once across all tiles
claims.claim: The existing workspace applies filters across all tiles without restricting that statement to the active tab.
claims.quote: Filters apply to all cards and visualizations on the current tab.
claims.fix: Replace 'filters applied once across all tiles' in What's changing with 'filters applied across all cards and visualisations on the current tab'. The roadmap-attributed summary may continue to describe the planned cascading filters.

claims.where: What's changing: saved workspace configurations; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The roadmap describes saved workspace configurations, reusable templates and views shared across the organisation.
claims.quote: Process Intelligence Studio saves your workspace configurations, allowing teams to create reusable analysis templates and share standardized views across the organization for consistent process monitoring and improvement tracking.
claims.fix: Move 'saved workspace configurations that can be reused as templates' out of the unqualified current-capabilities sentence and replace it with: 'The roadmap also describes saved workspace configurations that teams can reuse as analysis templates and share as standardised views.'

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap plans full workspace functionality for OCPM as well as traditional process models.
claims.quote:
The platform supports both traditional and object-centric process mining methodologies
Object-centric support: Extends full functionality to OCPM models

claims.claim: In OCPM, one event can relate to multiple business objects, including orders, invoices and payments.
claims.quote:
OCPM lets one event belong to multiple objects (and object types), keeping the full context intact.
Order O1, Invoice I1, Supplier Order SO1, Payment P1

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; rationale: risk
claims.claim: OCPM process models are created by ingesting object-centric event logs stored in Azure Data Lake Gen2 or OneLake.
claims.quote:
first create a process model by ingesting the object-centric event log (OCEL).
Then, store the resulting file in a CSV format in either Azure Data Lake Gen2 or OneLake.

claims.claim: Learn documents only the Process overview tab in the current OCPM preview.
claims.quote: In the preview of this feature, only the Process overview tab is available.

claims.claim: Learn documents only the Default view in the current OCPM preview.
claims.quote: In the preview of this feature, only the Default view is available.

claims.claim: Learn calls the existing analysis interface the process intelligence experience.
claims.quote: The new process intelligence experience is the next-generation interface for process analysis in Power Automate Process Mining.

claims.claim: Object-centric event logs can include business identifiers such as order and invoice IDs.
claims.quote: each row is an event (with activity and timestamp) and has one or more columns listing the object IDs per object type that the event touched (for example, Order=O2, Invoice=I1).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Environment Maker is a documented role for creating processes.
claims.quote: The Environment maker role can use the process mining capabilities to create, share, and contribute to processes.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The roadmap describes an analysis workspace rather than announcing an autonomous automation capability.
claims.quote: Process Intelligence Studio is a modern, flexible workspace designed for comprehensive process analysis. It provides a fully customizable analysis environment that combines multiple visualization and analysis components into cohesive, purpose-built workspaces.

claims.claim: Process mining has documented licensing within Power Automate.
claims.quote: Process mining is licensed as part of Microsoft Power Automate. Three Power Automate licenses relate to process mining, and a Power BI license is required for Power BI report customization.

claims.where: Governance controls prose: capacity from Premium licences
claims.claim: Power Automate Premium licences contribute process mining capacity.
claims.quote: Each Power Automate Premium license adds 50 MB of process mining capacity to a tenant-wide capacity pool up to a total of 100 GB.

claims.where: Governance controls prose: Process Mining add-on
claims.claim: The Power Automate Process Mining add-on contributes additional process mining capacity.
claims.quote:
The Process Mining add-on is a tenant-wide license that's available for the Power Automate Premium license. It offers:
An extra 100 GB of process mining capacity to the capacity pool, which users with the Power Automate Premium license can use.

claims.claim: Process mining capacity is pooled tenant-wide.
claims.quote: Each Power Automate Premium license adds 50 MB of process mining capacity to a tenant-wide capacity pool up to a total of 100 GB.

claims.claim: ProcessMiningDataStorage capacity can be allocated at environment scope.

ExternalCurrencyType

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Azure Data Lake storage; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Azure Data Lake storage carries storage costs.
claims.quote: To analyze differences in data storage prices, transaction prices, and storage capacity reservation pricing between accounts that have a flat namespace versus a hierarchical namespace, see Azure Data Lake Storage pricing.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/blobs/data-lake-storage-namespace#decide-whether-to-enable-a-hierarchical-namespace to sources for the Azure Data Lake storage-cost statement.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: OneLake storage; rationale: cost
claims.claim: OneLake storage carries storage costs.
claims.quote:
Storage tiers affect both your pay-as-you-go rate for OneLake storage and your Fabric Capacity Unit (CU) consumption for OneLake transactions:
Storage charges: The per-GB, per-month cost that's highest for hot storage and lowest for cold storage.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/onelake/onelake-storage-tiers#storage-tiers-and-onelake-consumption to sources for the OneLake storage-cost statement.

claims.claim: The allocation tutorial shows how to allocate add-ons using a flow.
claims.quote:
Allocate an add-on using Power Automate flows or Logic Apps
Add a new action to the canvas, searching for "Allocate and deallocate the currencies for the environment". Set the parameters to higher numeric values to perform assignment.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to review Environment Maker assignments and process-data access, but neither control has a corresponding table row.
claims.quote:
Check who holds the Environment Maker role.
Review who can see sensitive process data.
The table instead lists capacity allocation, who may allocate capacity, and an undocumented feature switch.
claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullets 'Check who holds the Environment Maker role' and 'Review who can see sensitive process data' to eliminate instructions for controls not represented in the table; do not add unverified control rows.
